Given: $P \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$be the foot of the perpendicular from the point $Q \left(1, 2, 3\right)$ on the line $\dfrac{x + 3}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 4}{3}$

So, any point on the line is given by \left(5\lambda - 3, 2\lambda + 1, 3\lambda - 4\right)$, so let the point be $P \left($5\lambda - 3, 2\lambda + 1, 3\lambda - 4\right)$

Now, direction ratio of $PQ = \left($5\lambda - 4, 2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda - 7\right)$

Now, the line and $PQ$ will be perpendicular,

So, 5\left($5\lambda - 4\right) + $2\left($2\lambda - 1\right) + $3\left($3\lambda - 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ 38\lambda - 43 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{43}{38}$

So, the point P\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right) =$P \left(5 \times $\dfrac{43}{38} -$3, 2 \times $\dfrac{43}{38} +$1, 3 \times $\dfrac{43}{38} -$4\right)$

Then $19\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) =19 \left[$5 $\times \dfrac{43}{38} -$3 + 2 $\times \dfrac{43}{38} +$1 + 3 $\times \dfrac{43}{38} -$4\right]$

$⇒ 19 \left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) =$19 \left[\dfrac{101 + 124 - 23}{38}\right]$

$⇒ 19\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) =101$

$

The given lines are$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{0} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z + 6}{1}$and~$\dfrac{x + \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 6}{0}$

We know that the shortest distance between two lines is~$d = \left|\left(\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{n}1 \times \overset{→}{n}2\right)\left|\overset{→}{n}$1 $\times \overset{→}{n}$2\right|\right| & d = $13\left(\text{given}\right)

$⇒ \overset{→}{n}1 $\times \overset{→}{n}$2 = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } 1 \\ 3 \text{ and } - 4 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}$\right|= 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}$

Now using the above formula of distance we get,

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{( 2\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot ( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} )}{16 + 9 + 144}\right| =$13$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{( 2\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot ( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} )}{13}\right| =$13$

$⇒ \left|$8\lambda + 9 + 144\right| = 169$

$⇒ \left|$8\lambda + 153\right| = 169$

$⇒ 8\lambda = $\pm$169 - 153$

$⇒ \lambda = $\dfrac{16}{8}, \dfrac{- 322}{8}

$⇒ $8\left|\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s}\lambda\right| =8\left|\dfrac{16}{8} - \dfrac{322}{8}\right| =$306

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let the shortest distance between the lines $L: \dfrac{x - 5}{- 2} = \dfrac{y - \lambda}{0} = \dfrac{z + \lambda}{1}, \lambda \ge 0$~and ${L}_{1}: x + 1 = y - 1 = 4 - z$~be $2\sqrt{6}$. If $( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ lies on $L$, then which of the following is NOT possible?

questions.solution:
Given equations of lines are

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x + 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{- 1}$

Here,

$\overset{→}{b1} \times \overset{→}{b2} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b1} \times \overset{→}{b2} = - \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\overset{→}{a2} - \overset{→}{a1} = 6\overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \lambda - 4\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∵$~Shortest distance is~$2\sqrt{6}$.

$⇒ 2\sqrt{6} = \left|\dfrac{- 6 - \lambda + 1 + 2\lambda + 8}{1 + 1 + 4}\right|$

$⇒ | \lambda + 3 | = 12 ⇒ \lambda = 9, - 15$

$⇒ \alpha = - 2k + 5, \gamma = k - \lambda$~where~$k \in R$

So,

$\alpha + 2\gamma = 5 - 2\lambda = - 13, 35$

questions.q: Let $PQR$ be a triangle with $R ( - 1, 4, 2 )$. Suppose $M ( 2, 1, 2 )$ is the mid point of $PQ$. The distance of the centroid of $∆ PQR$ from the point of intersection of the line $\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{- 1}$ and $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + 3}{- 3} = \dfrac{z + 1}{1}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{- 1}$ and $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + 3}{- 3} = \dfrac{z + 1}{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{- 1} = k \left(\text{let}\right)$

$⇒ x = 2, y = 2k, z = - k + 3 . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + 3}{- 3} = \dfrac{z + 1}{1} = \lambda \left(\text{let}\right)$

$⇒ x = \lambda + 1, y = - 3\lambda - 3 . z = \lambda - 1 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Using \left($i\right)\text{and}\left($ii\right)$,

$⇒ 2 = \lambda + 1, 2k = - 3\lambda - 3$

$⇒ \lambda = 1, 2k = - 3 - 3$

$⇒ \lambda = 1, k = - 3$

$⇒ x = 2, y = - 6, z = 0$

So, the intersection point of two given lines is \left(2, - 6, 0\right)$.

Now, we know that centroid $G$ divides $MR$ (median) in the ratio $1: 2$.

So, by using section formula, $G ≡ \left(\dfrac{1 \times - 1 + 2 \times 2}{3}, \dfrac{1 \times 4 + 2 \times 1}{3}, \dfrac{1 \times 2 + 2 \times 2}{3}\right)$

So, centroid is $G ( 1, 2, 2 )$.

Let $A$ be the point of intersection of given lines.

$⇒ AG = \sqrt{\left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(2 + 6\right)2 + \left(2 - 0\right)2}$

$⇒ AG = \sqrt{1 + 64 + 4}$

$⇒ AG = \sqrt{69}$

questions.q: A line passes through $A  \left(4, - 6, - 2\right)$ and $B  \left(16, - 2, 4\right)$. The point $P  \left(a, b, c\right)$ where $a, b, c$ are non-negative integers, on the line $AB$ lies at a distance of $21$ units, from the point $A$. The distance between the points $P  \left($a, b, c\right)$ and $Q  \left($4, - 12, 3\right) is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

A line passes through $A \left(4, - 6, - 2\right)$ and $B \left(16, - 2, 4\right)$,

So, the equation of line will be $\dfrac{x - 4}{12} = \dfrac{x + 6}{4} = \dfrac{z + 2}{6}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 4}{6} = \dfrac{x + 6}{2} = \dfrac{z + 2}{3}$

So, the direction cosines will be $\dfrac{6}{{6}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {3}^{2}}, \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{{6}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {3}^{2}}}, \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{{6}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {3}^{2}}}$

$≡ \dfrac{6}{7}, \dfrac{2}{7}, \dfrac{3}{7}$

Now, given point $P \left(a, b, c\right)$ lies on the line $AB$ and at a distance of $21$ from point $A$

So, by using the equation of line $AB$ we get,

$⇒ $\dfrac{a - 4}{\dfrac{6}{7}} = \dfrac{b + 6}{\dfrac{2}{7}} = \dfrac{c + 2}{\dfrac{3}{7}} =$21$

$⇒ \left(21 \times $\dfrac{6}{7} +$4, $\dfrac{2}{7} \times$21 - 6, $\dfrac{3}{7} \times$21 - 2\right) ≡ \left($a, b, c\right)$

$⇒ \left($22, 0, 7\right) ≡ \left(a, b, c\right)$

Hence, the distance between $P \left(22, 0, 7\right) & Q \left(4, - 12, 3\right)$ is given by, $\sqrt{324 + 144 + 16} =22$

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines& $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 6}{2}$~and~$\dfrac{x - 6}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{0}$& is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given equations are

$\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 6}{2}$~is passing through a point~ \left(2, - 1, 6\right)$~and it's direction ratios are~$3, 2, 2$.

So,~

$\overset{→}{a}1 = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}1 = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\dfrac{x - 6}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{0}$~is passing through a point~ \left(6, 1, - 8\right)$~and it's direction ratios are~$3, - 2, 0$.

$\overset{→}{a}2 = 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}2 = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}$

Now,

$\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1 = 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & 0\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = 4\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{16 + 36 + 144} = 14$

We know that the shortest distance between two skew lines is~\left|\left(\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right)\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}\right)}{14}\right|$

$= \left|16 + 12 + 168\right|14 = 14$ \text{ and } units

$

questions.q: Let a line passing through the point $( - 1, 2, 3 )$ intersect the lines ${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 2}$ at $M ( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ and ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x + 2}{- 3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{4}$ at $N ( a, b, c )$. Then the value of $\dfrac{( \alpha + \beta + \gamma{)}^{2}}{( a + b + c{)}^{2}}$ equals ________________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Let,

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 2} = \lambda$

$⇒ M ( 3\lambda + 1, 2\lambda + 2, - 2\lambda - 1 ) ≡ M \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)

$⇒ $\alpha + \beta + \gamma =$3\lambda + 2$

Also, ${L}_{2}: $\dfrac{x + 2}{- 3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{4} = \mu

$⇒ N ( - 3\mu - 2, - 2\mu + 2, 4\mu + 1 ) ≡ N \left(a, b, c\right)$

$⇒ a + b + c = - \mu + 1$

Now, from the above diagram, we can see $MN$ lie on the same line,

So, $\dfrac{3\lambda + 2}{- 3\mu - 1} = \dfrac{2\lambda}{- 2\mu} = \dfrac{- 2\lambda - 4}{4\mu - 2}$

Now, solving $\dfrac{3\lambda + 2}{- 3\mu - 1} = \dfrac{2\lambda}{- 2\mu}$

$⇒ 3\lambda\mu + 2\mu = 3\lambda\mu + \lambda$

$⇒ 2\mu = \lambda . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, solving \dfrac{2\lambda}{- 2\mu} = \dfrac{- 2\lambda - 4}{4\mu - 2}we get,

$⇒ 2\lambda\mu - \lambda = \lambda\mu + 2\mu$

$⇒ \lambda\mu = \lambda + 2\mu$

$⇒ \lambda\mu = 2\$lambda\left\{\text{as}$2\mu = \lambda\right\}

$⇒ \mu = 2 ( \lambda \ne 0 )$

$⇒ \lambda = $4\left\{\text{from equation}\left($i\right)\right\}

Hence, \alpha + \beta + \gamma =$14$ and $a + b + c = - 1$

So, $\dfrac{( \alpha + \beta + \gamma{)}^{2}}{( a + b + c{)}^{2}} =196$
